text:
Elena (Finance): Team, incoming oddball invoice that affects month/quarter close — need opinions. Invoice #497732 is for EUR 115,000 (converted to USD on invoice at 1.09 = $125,350.00). Service period: 2026-02-20 -> 2026-03-31. Vendor posted late; arrived 2026-04-03. Do we treat as: 1) split across Feb & Mar deferrals by service days, or 2) prior-period adjustment to March only, or 3) book as April accrual with disclosure? @Sam (Audit) @Devon (Billing) @Jon (RevenueOps)

invoice-bot: Invoice #497732 uploaded: https://invoices.redwood.local/497732. Invoice date 2026-04-03. Amount EUR 115,000 / USD 125,350.00. Attached: inv_497732.pdf.

Devon (Billing): Pulled usage detail. It's mostly recurring model serving fees tied to daily usage. Breakdown by service days: Feb 20-28 = 9 days (~28% of service days), Mar 1-31 = 31 days (~72%). CSV fragment:
customer_id,usage_date,tokens,amount_usd
ORCHID-2,2026-03-15,7_200_000,31_200.00
TIDE-8,2026-02-25,1_100_000,4_950.00
MISC-POOL,2026-03-28,12_000_000,89_200.00
Totals align to invoice after FX. No duplicates.

Jon (RevenueOps): Matching principle: recognize revenue in the period services were rendered. Given mixed period, we should split the deferral/amortization across Feb and Mar by service-day proportion. Since Feb is in prior month (and prior close may be complete), this will be a prior-period adjustment for Feb for the 9-day portion and regular March deferral for the remainder. We'll need a memo documenting allocation method and FX rate used.

Sam (Audit): Agree with split allocation across service days. Requirements: 1) calculation workpaper with day counts and per-customer mapping, 2) FX documentation showing rate/time of conversion and policy for exchange variance, 3) approver sign-offs. For the Feb portion, tag JE as "post-close prior period" and include lead schedules. Also confirm whether the FX gain/loss posts to P&L or is captured in COGS.

Priya (Sales Ops): Heads-up: ORCHID-2 and TIDE-8 were in our Feb pricing experiment; ORCHID-2 is eligible for a retro credit of $3,500, TIDE-8 for $800. We prefer to issue the credits on the next customer invoice (April) for clarity. How do we reflect those credits if we pull part of the invoice into Feb?

Elena (Finance): Options: A) Gross allocation to Feb & Mar and record Customer Credit Liabilities for retro credits (preserve gross deferral), B) Net credits against AR in Feb (reduces AR prior-period), or C) Book gross and hold credits until applied in April (credit liability). Audit has previously preferred A for traceability.

Devon (Billing): Practically, easiest is A: split gross by service days into Feb & Mar deferral buckets, and set Customer Credit Liabilities per customer (ORCHID-2 $3,500, TIDE-8 $800). JE sketches:
Date 2026-02-28 (prior-period adj for Feb portion)
Dr Accounts Receivable 35,098.00
  Cr Deferred Revenue 31,598.00
  Cr Customer Credit Liability 3,500.00
(allocates 28% of invoice to Feb; ORCHID-2 credit reserved)

Date 2026-03-31
Dr Accounts Receivable 90,252.00
  Cr Deferred Revenue 86,452.00
  Cr Customer Credit Liability 3,800.00
(allocates remaining 72% to Mar; TIDE-8 and remainder reserved)
Note: FX already converted on invoice, but if bank conversion differs when we pay, we'll book exchange variance to COGS.

Sam (Audit): Confirming approach A is acceptable. Please include FX variance policy excerpt in memo. Also make sure the Feb JE is clearly labeled as a post-close prior period adjustment and include the calculation file with day-weighted allocation and customer-level credits.

Jon (RevenueOps): I'll update the revenue schedule: create two prior-period lines linking to invoice 497732 (Feb portion flagged post-close) with amortization consistent with our consumption pattern. Also will add a note to the close retrospective to tighten vendor invoice SLA and FX timing to avoid future splits.

Priya (Sales Ops): Agrees with reserving customer credits as liabilities and applying credits on April invoices. Will prepare customer comms templates for ORCHID-2 and TIDE-8 so Billing can attach when credit is issued.

Elena (Finance): Action items: 1) I'll draft the memo with allocation table, FX rate, and JE drafts (target: EOD), 2) @Devon to prepare and tag Feb prior-period JE for posting after approvals, 3) @Jon to update revenue schedule and forecasts, 4) @Priya to prepare credit comms.

Sam (Audit): Approve proceeding on that plan. Please route memo to audit@redwood.com and cc finance@redwood.com. Mark Feb JE as "post-close prior period".

Devon (Billing): Will prepare calculation workbook and the two JEs. I'll attach the invoice PDF and the billing extract.

Elena (Finance): Thanks all. Posting memo link here when done and then will close thread.
